All three voters agree and I checked the sources myself. primary is the m=1 homogeneous modal solution with z₊(0)=P(0), z₋(0)=0, and its ambient image solves t'=A_Φt−dt. referenceP is (7.12). primary_bounds gives uniform cP≤x≤CP and y/x=h+O(1/S), with h=c0√(1+s²). FamilyData.coefficientControl discharges its hypotheses for the actual frames. FamilyData.pulse_jets gives the C S^m P derivative bounds, and phasePressure_carrier_jets the √ε pressure gain. Every gap is packaging: an abstract lemma plus an instantiation, normalized θ, docstring numbering, and a K orientation convention. Two corrections to the auditor's descriptions: canonicalPrimaryPulse_bounds concludes Gaussian envelopes, and primary_ratio_error is a vector bound. Neither changes the verdict.

findings.summary: No single declaration states (7.21) for the actual pulses. The bound is proved abstractly in primary_bounds, and its hypotheses are discharged by FamilyData.coefficientControl only inside proofs. The exposed ratio is a vector bound, and the pressure gain is instantiated only on amplitude-weighted pulses.
The derivative bounds are stated on the normalized open slot θ=v/L∈(0,1), with joint jets in (slow point, θ) and weight P(Lθ). The paper states them in v on [0,L_s].
Docstrings cite '(28)' and '(27)' from an older manuscript numbering, rather than (7.21) and the projected equation in (7.13).

The reference transverse direction has the opposite orientation: in Lean K = (N_z, −N_θ) and N_a = quarterTurn(K_a); in the paper K = (−N_z, N_θ) and N_a = −quarterTurn(K_a). So Lean's sign σ pulse is the paper's (−σ) pulse with a negated phase.
